scenes.heading: Managing multiple client accounts without burning out

sents.d: Managing multiple client accounts without burning out
Systemizing repetitive tasks across accounts protects your time as you grow.

Managing several client accounts individually, from scratch each time, doesn't scale — using a shared content calendar and scheduling tool across all clients centralizes the repetitive parts of the work.

Batching similar tasks across all clients (writing all captions in one sitting, scheduling all posts in another) tends to be more efficient than fully completing one client's month before starting the next.

Setting a maximum number of active client accounts based on your actual available hours — rather than accepting every new client that inquires — protects service quality and prevents the kind of overload that leads to missed posts or slow response times.

take: Centralize tools, batch tasks and cap how many clients you take.
